Bijan Robinson finished last season with 1,478 rushing yards and 820 receiving yards.

Atlanta Falcons +6.5

Kyle Pitts Sr. offers another option against a Pittsburgh defense that allowed opposing tight ends 6.4 receptions per game last season.

The Yankees’ starter enters with a 2.01 ERA and 0.92 WHIP, compared with 3.81 and 1.29 for the Mets’ starter.

Yankees ML

Buffalo allowed 5.1 yards per carry last season, and David Montgomery and Woody Marks give the Texans a way to test that vulnerability.

Houston Texans ML

Philadelphia’s extra-inning Friday was followed by an emergency bullpen game Saturday, leaving multiple relievers with consecutive appearances and one with a 39-pitch outing.

Braves ML

St. Louis’s starter has a 3.92 ERA and 1.25 WHIP over 154.0 innings; Chicago’s has a 6.93 ERA and 1.38 WHIP over 24.2 innings.

Cardinals ML

Love finished last season with 23 touchdowns against 6 interceptions, and the Packers converted 48.8% of their third downs.

Green Bay Packers +1.5

Las Vegas has a legitimate answer: Ashton Jeanty against a Miami defense that allowed 132.4 rushing yards per game last season.

Miami Dolphins +3

The Raiders have rebuilt their offensive line, and their own defense allowed the second-fewest rushing yards per attempt in 2025.

San Diego’s starter adds an encouraging foundation: 26 strikeouts against 6 walks in 21.0 innings, with a 0.95 WHIP.

San Diego Padres ML

The Giants’ closer-type option has a 4.85 ERA and 1.51 WHIP, compared with a 1.14 ERA and 0.85 WHIP for San Diego’s closer.
